newsitem.title: FINLAND: Thin Helsinki edges higher amid overseas jitters.
newsitem.headline: Thin Helsinki edges higher amid overseas jitters.

text.p: Shares closed a shade higher on Thursday, after struggling to hold gains in thin trade dampened by jitters on European financial markets, brokers said.
The FOX stock futures index ended just barely into positive ground, up 0.01 percent at 1,062.61, while the HEX gained 0.16 percent to 3,071.24 points.

"Economic and monetary union is at stake in Sweden, and the French leftists' success has made Europe cautious," one broker said. Amidst those jitters, the market was waiting for direction from the United States, another said.
The market drew support from Nokia, which ended 2.50 markka higher at 348.50 in fair 100 million markka volume.
Sporting goods group Amer added 4.40 markka to end at 103.40 in lively 33 million markka dealings after reporting improved four-month performance, though still showing a loss.

Amer's January-April loss of 49 million markka was smaller than the median of analysts' forecasts in a Reuters poll at 53 million markka. Brokers said the share was also helped by Amer's positive comments on the outlook for its main divisions.
But views on Amer were mixed. "A loss is a loss. It should start to make a profit soon," one broker said.
Industrial crane builder Konecranes fell 3.30 markka to 192.50 markka after reporting four-month profits up 2.5 percent to 37 million markka, but slightly below the median of analysts' forecasts.
"The result was below expectations, and the company did not give a clear enough vision of the future," one broker said.
Small cap Lassila & Tikanoja ended up 10.00 markka at 410.00 after reporting sharply higher four-month profits.
Forestries underperformed the market, with UPM off 0.70 markka at 118.30 in sturdy 74 million markka volume.
Brokers said trade could remain subdued ahead of interim results from heavyweights Valmet and Outokumpu next week.
